skada.tutorial.section.1.title: What is Skada?
skada.tutorial.section.1.body.1: Skada is a combat overhaul mod that fundamentally changes how damage works in Minecraft.
skada.tutorial.section.1.body.2: Every weapon attack falls into one of three Combat Types — Slash, Thrust, or Strike — and deals one or more Elemental damage types such as Heat, Cold, Lightning, or Ender. Armours, enchantments, and status effects each provide their own ratings against these damage types and elements. This means the Diamond Sword you have equipped isn’t just “dealing damage” — it is specifically dealing Slash damage with a Physical edge, and a creature’s armour may resist or amplify that depending on its own ratings.
skada.tutorial.section.1.body.3: The Journal is your primary window into all of this. Open it with the key bound to Open Journal (default: G). It contains four pages: Player Stats, Damage Info, a Bestiary, and this Tutorial.
skada.tutorial.section.2.title: Combat Types
skada.tutorial.section.2.body.1: There are three Combat Types, each describing the mechanical character of an attack.
skada.tutorial.section.2.body.2: Slash attacks sweep wide and powerful blows. Swords and Axes deal Slash damage. This is the most common damage type, and most armours provide moderate Slash resistance.
skada.tutorial.section.2.body.3: Thrust attacks concentrate force into a single piercing point. Tridents and some daggers deal Thrust damage. Thrust attacks tend to ignore more armour than Slash, making them effective against heavily armoured foes.
skada.tutorial.section.2.body.4: Strike attacks bring blunt, concussive force. Maces, Hammers, and Shovels deal Strike damage. Strike damage scales with the target’s Wither resistance, making it especially lethal against undead and withered entities.
skada.tutorial.section.2.body.5: Your current weapon’s combat type is shown in its tooltip and in the Damage Info page of your Journal.
skada.tutorial.section.3.title: Elements
skada.tutorial.section.3.body.1: Beyond the physical damage types, Skada adds a full elemental system. Every weapon carries an Element Power Budget that determines how much elemental damage it can deal, distributed across one or more elements.
skada.tutorial.section.3.body.2: The seven elements are: Heat, Cold, Lightning, Ender, Wither, Aether, and Physical. Each creature in the world has its own elemental resistance profile — fire-resistant creatures take reduced Heat damage, undead are especially vulnerable to Wither, and aquatic mobs are typically weak to Lightning.
skada.tutorial.section.3.body.3: As you fight different creatures, the Bestiary records their elemental strengths and weaknesses. Check it before entering a difficult area — knowing whether a mob resists your weapon’s element can be the difference between a smooth fight and a deadly one.
skada.tutorial.section.4.title: The Journal
skada.tutorial.section.4.body.1: The Journal tracks everything combat-related. Open it by pressing G (or your configured key) while holding any weapon. It has four pages:
skada.tutorial.section.4.body.2: Player — Displays your current elemental and combat-type resistances alongside your core stats (Health, Armour, Toughness, Speed). Use this page to identify gaps in your defences.
skada.tutorial.section.4.body.3: Damage Info — Shows a detailed breakdown of your held weapon: its combat types, reach, weight, and elemental profile. Tap your attack-type key to cycle between its available attack modes and see how each one differs.
skada.tutorial.section.4.body.4: Bestiary — Automatically records creatures you have damaged or killed. Each entry lists their combat type, elemental affinities, and raw stat readings. Filter by dimension and aggression type to find what you are looking for.
skada.tutorial.section.5.title: Getting Started
skada.tutorial.section.5.body.1: Here are a few tips to get the most out of Skada:
skada.tutorial.section.5.body.2: Check your resists. Open the Journal and review your elemental resistances before exploring a new dimension or boss arena. Skada expects you to build defensively, not just offensively.
skada.tutorial.section.5.body.3: Match your weapon to the enemy. Open the Bestiary, find the creature you are about to fight, and compare its weaknesses to your weapon’s combat type and elements. Switching weapons before a difficult fight is a legitimate strategy.
skada.tutorial.section.5.body.4: The attack-type key is your most important tool. By default, tapping the Cycle Attack Type key while holding a weapon switches between its available attack modes. Each mode has different damage, reach, and elemental distribution — learn which mode fits your situation.
skada.tutorial.section.5.body.5: Armour matters differently now. Each armour piece contributes both combat-type and elemental resistance. A full set of Netherite is not just defence — it is a specific resistance profile. Enchantments and mob effects can shift that profile further.
skada.tutorial.section.5.body.6: Skada is designed to be readable on the fly. Trust the Journal, read the Bestiary, and adapt your loadout to each fight.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.allay.desc: The allay is a flying passive mob that collects and delivers items for any player that gives it something or any note block it hears recently playing.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.axolotl.desc: An axolotl is a passive bucketable aquatic mob found in lush caves. Axolotls attack fish, squid, drowned, and guardians; this makes axolotls useful for assisting with aquatic combat. Axolotls also grant players regeneration effects.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.bat.desc: A bat is a flying ambient passive mob that spawns in dark areas underground in caves.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.bee.desc: Bees are flying neutral mobs that live in bee nests and beehives. Bees pollinate flowers and, when they do, add honey to their home when they return to it. When full, bee nests or beehives can be harvested with shears for honeycombs or glass bottles for honey bottles. If provoked by being attacked or breaking or harvesting their hive or nest without the correct precautions, bees suicidally attack in a swarm.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.blaze.desc: A blaze is a hostile mob that spawns in nether fortresses and is the only source of blaze rods. Blazes attack at range by firing a trio of fireballs or can attack the player that gets too close to them with their spinning rods.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.camel.desc: A camel is a passive mob found in deserts and desert villages and that can be saddled and ridden by up to two players at once. A camel is tall enough that its riders cannot be reached from the ground by a few melee-attacking harmful mobs, who do not attack the camel.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.cat.desc: A cat is a passive mob found in villages and swamp huts. They can be tamed and used to repel creepers and phantoms.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.cave_spider.des: Cave spiders are small variants of the spider that inflict Poison with their attacks. They are exclusively spawned by monster spawners found in mineshafts.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.chicken.desc: The chicken is a passive mob found in grass biomes and the main source of raw chicken, feathers, and eggs. A chicken, like most animals, can be attached to a lead.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.cod.desc: Cod are common bucketable aquatic passive mobs found in oceans, and a source of raw cod and, occasionally, bones or bone meal.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.cow.desc: A cow is a passive mob and a source of leather, beef and milk.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.creeper.desc: A creeper is a common hostile mob that silently approaches players and then explodes, which can destroy blocks and kill unarmored players on any difficulty.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.dolphin.desc: Dolphins are neutral mobs that live in non-frozen oceans, which grant a speed boost to players that swim near them.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.donkey.desc: Donkeys are variants of horses that, when tamed, can be ridden and equipped with chests.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.drowned.desc: Drowned are common neutral underwater zombie variants that spawn in oceans, rivers and dripstone caves, or when zombies drown. They usually attack through melee attacks, but may also come armed with tridents that they throw. They are the only source of tridents, and the only renewable source of copper.
An elder guardian is a stronger and larger variant of the guardian, and the largest aquatic mob. It attacks the same way as a normal guardian, but also applies Mining Fatigue to players in a large radius around itself. They are only found in ocean monuments; three of them generate in each one.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.ender_dragon.de: The ender dragon is a giant flying hostile boss mob found when first entering the End. She is the largest naturally spawning mob in the game.

She guards access to the end gateways that provide entry to the outer end islands in addition to the exit portal that allows return to the Overworld as well as access to the end credits of Minecraft. Because of this, she is known by most Minecraft fans as the 'final boss' of the game. Her attacks involve charging at the player and her unique dragon acid attacks.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.enderman.desc: The Enderman is a tall neutral mob found in all three dimensions. Endermen normally ignore players and lazily amble about, but they will swiftly walk to attack those that damage it or look directly at its face. Endermen teleport to avoid water (which harms them), projectiles and some other damage sources, and they occasionally pick up certain blocks. They will also teleport more rapidly in sunlight.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.endermite.desc: An endermite is the smallest hostile mob. An endermite may spawn when a player throws an ender pearl. They attack by biting the player. Endermen are hostile toward endermites.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.evoker.desc: An evoker is a spell-casting illager found in woodland mansions and raids, and the only source of the totem of undying. It uses two spells to attack; one that summons armor-piercing fangs and one that summons vexes.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.fox.desc: A fox is a neutral mob that spawns in taigas, old growth taigas, snowy taigas and mountain groves. They are able to carry a single item in their mouth, but prefer food over other items.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.frog.desc: A frog is a passive mob found in swamps. Frogs eat small slimes and magma cubes. A frog can produce one of three kinds of froglights from eating magma cubes, depending on the type of frog.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.ghast.desc: Ghasts are large white floating ghost-like hostile mobs that live in the Nether and shoot explosive fireballs at the player.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.giant.desc: Giants are unused, over-sized mobs that look like zombies.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.glow_squid.desc: The glow squid is a variant of squid found in dark underwater areas, typically in ocean depths, ravines and underground lakes. It has an aqua luminescent texture. The mob originates from Minecraft Earth.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.goat.desc: A goat is a neutral mob found in certain mountainous biomes. Goats can jump especially high, and ram mobs. They are a source of goat horns and milk.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.guardian.desc: Guardians are pufferfish-like hostile mobs that spawn in and around ocean monuments. They attack with a slow-charging laser beam, and inflict retaliatory damage when damaged by a melee attack.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.hoglin.desc: A hoglin is a breedable hostile mob found in the Nether, and a source of porkchops and leather. A hoglin attacks by thrusting its tusks upward, which can also launch its target a short distance into the air. Hoglins are repelled by warped fungi that is placed in the world as well as active nether portals and respawn anchors. They were originaly named the piglin beast in Minecon 2019 but was changed to hoglin a month later
skada.bestiary.minecraft.horse.desc: Horses are passive mobs that can be ridden when tamed and saddled.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.husk.desc: A husk is a variant of a zombie that spawns in deserts. They function similar to zombies, except they do not burn in sunlight and inflict Hunger with their unarmed attacks.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.illusioner.desc: The illusioner is an unused illager armed with a bow. It attacks using illusions and can also fire arrows.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.llama.desc: A llama is a tamable neutral mob used to transport large shipments of items using caravans.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.iron_golem.desc: An iron golem is a buildable neutral mob that attacks monsters with its arms, knocking them into the air. Iron golems created by villagers or spawned in villages patrol their village, and may attack players that attack it or have a low popularity or reputation with their village.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.magma_cube.desc: A magma cube is a hostile mob found in the Nether. A magma cube behaves similarly to a slime, but is fireproof, jumps higher and less often, and deals more damage.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.mooshroom.desc: Mooshrooms are mushroom-covered variants of cows exclusive to the rare mushroom fields biome. Although they look similar to cows, they are not cows.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.mule.desc: Mules are infertile offspring of horses and donkeys that, when tamed, can be ridden and equipped with chests.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.ocelot.desc: An ocelot is a passive mob that may be found in jungles.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.panda.desc: A panda is a rare neutral mob that resides in jungles. Certain aspects of a panda's behavior and appearance vary depending on its personality.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.parrot.desc: A parrot is a tameable passive mob that spawns in jungle biomes. Parrots can imitate sounds of nearby monsters and can also perch on the player's shoulders.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.phantom.desc: Phantoms are flying undead hostile mobs that spawn in the night sky when the player has not laid in a bed or died for three or more in-game days. They attack by diving at the player from the sky to bite them. Usually, they appear in trios.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.pig.desc: A pig is a passive mob found commonly in most grass biomes, though they also can also spawn in the Taiga biomes, the Badlands, Savanna, and Jungle biomes with seperate variants. Pigs are a source of porkchops and can be equipped with a saddle to be driven.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.piglin.desc: A piglin is a neutral mob found in the Nether. It is hostile to players unless they wear at least one piece of golden armor. It can be given gold ingots to barter for various items. It wields either a golden sword or a crossbow, and uses either melee or ranged attacks, respectively.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.piglin_brute.de: A piglin brute is a hostile and stronger variant of piglins that appears in all types of bastion remnants. Unlike regular piglins, they do not barter or retreat, and they cannot be distracted with gold. Instead, they always charge at the player on sight with their golden axes.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.pillager.desc: Pillagers are hostile mobs armed with crossbows found in wandering patrols, in pillager outposts, or as participants in raid events. They attack by firing arrows at the player.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.polar_bear.desc: Polar bears are neutral mobs that live in icy biomes.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.pufferfish.desc: Pufferfish are bucketable aquatic mobs found in oceans. Although they never seek out mobs to attack, they will defensively inflate themselves when approached too closely by players, axolotls or non-aquatic mobs, dealing damage and inflicting Poison on them.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.rabbit.desc: A rabbit is an uncommon passive mob and is a source of rabbit's foot, rabbit hide, and raw rabbit.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.ravager.desc: Ravagers are large hostile mobs that only spawn alongside illagers in raids. They attack players, adult villagers, wandering traders and iron golems by running at them and biting them. They can be briefly stunned by being blocked with a shield, but after recovering they will roar, damaging and knocking away all nearby entities.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.salmon.desc: Salmon are common bucketable aquatic passive mobs found in oceans and rivers, and a source of raw salmon, and occasionally, bones or bone meal.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.sheep.desc: Sheep are common passive mobs that supply wool and mutton and are found in many of the grassy biomes. Sheep can be attached to a lead.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.shulker.desc: A shulker is a box-shaped hostile mob found in end cities. It hides in its shell to protect itself and blend in with its surroundings. It attacks by shooting homing bullets at the player which inflict Levitation. It is the only source of shulker shells, which are used to craft shulker boxes.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.silverfish.desc: Silverfish are small hostile mobs that infest stone and deepslate blocks in mountains, strongholds, igloo basements and woodland mansions. They crawl at their targets to bite them, and attacking them will incite other nearby silverfish to emerge from their blocks and attack the aggressor. Silverfish are also the only hostile mob that is not imaginary.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.skeleton.desc: Skeletons are undead common hostile mobs that perform ranged attacks with a bow by shooting arrows.
A Skeleton Horse is an undead neutral variant of the horse. It sometimes spawns when lightning strikes.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.slime.desc: Slimes are bouncy, cube-shaped hostile mobs that spawn deep underground in particular chunks, or in swamp biomes. They attack by jumping at their targets. They come in three sizes, the larger slimes can split into smaller ones when they die.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.sniffer.desc: A sniffer is an ancient passive mob that does not spawn naturally, and can only be hatched from sniffer eggs. It sniffs out and digs out seeds for various unique decorative plants out of dirt, grass, and moss blocks.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.snow_golem.desc: A snow golem is a buildable passive mob that throws snowballs at monsters, which provokes them into attacking it. Depending on the biome temperature it will also either produce a trail of snow, or take heat damage and die.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.spider.desc: A spider is a neutral mob that attacks the player in dark areas. Spiders attack by biting the target, and they can also climb walls and lunge at them.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.squid.desc: A squid is a common passive aquatic mob that spawns in rivers and oceans.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.stray.desc: A stray is a variant of a skeleton that spawns in a few snow-covered biomes. They behave similarly to skeletons, except they fire tipped arrows of Slowness from their bows.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.strider.desc: Striders are passive mobs native to the Nether. They can walk on lava, and be saddled and ridden by the player. A warped fungus on a stick is needed to control a strider, similar to how a pig is controlled by a carrot on a stick.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.tadpole.desc: A tadpole is a bucketable aquatic baby passive mob hatched from frogspawn. They mature into one of the three frog variants depending on the biome in which they mature.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.tropical_fish.d: Tropical Fish are common bucketable aquatic passive mobs found in oceans, mangrove swamps and lush caves. There are 2,700 naturally occurring variants of tropical fish of different colors and shapes with unique names.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.turtle.desc: A turtle, also known as a sea turtle, is a common, semi-aquatic passive mob found in beach biomes. They are the only source of scutes, which drop from baby turtles when they mature into adults.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.vex.desc: The vex is a small flying hostile mob. It wields an iron sword, can phase through walls, and is only summoned as one of the evoker's attacks. They attack by lunging at their targets with their sword.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.vindicator.desc: A vindicator is an illager equipped with an iron axe. Vindicators appear in woodland mansions and participate in raids. It sprints towards its targets to attack them with its axe.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.villager.desc: Villagers are passive mobs that inhabit villages, work at their professions, breed, and interact with each other. Villagers' outfits vary according to their biome, and adult villagers' outfits vary depending on their occupation. A player can trade with them using emeralds as currency.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.wandering_trade: The wandering trader is a passive mob that randomly spawns near the player. It can trade, making natural items more available, less dangerous to obtain, and in some cases, renewable.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.warden.desc.1: The warden is an extremely powerful hostile mob summoned by sculk shriekers in the deep dark biome. It attacks by swinging its arms downward, dealing the strongest melee damage of all mobs, and can also release a sonic boom attack that immediately strikes the target, piercing through obstacles and deals damage that cannot be reduced except by the Resistance effect.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.warden.desc.2: Wardens are completely blind and rely on vibrations, smell, and touch to detect players and mobs, and can therefore be evaded via sneaking, diversions (snowballs, arrows, etc.) and wool.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.witch.desc: The witch is a hostile mob that uses potions in combat, both in the form of weapons as splash potions and in the form of drinkable potions for defense.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.wither.desc.1: The wither is a player-constructed and highly destructive undead hostile boss mob that can hover in mid-air and fire barrages of explosive wither skulls at its target (which happens to be everything living).
skada.bestiary.minecraft.wither.desc.2: It is the only source of nether stars, which are used to craft beacons.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.wither_skeleton: Wither skeletons are tall black variants of skeletons equipped with stone swords that inflict the poison-like Wither effect. They are found exclusively in nether fortresses and are the only source of wither skeleton skulls, as well as the only renewable source of coal.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.wolf.desc: A wolf is a neutral mob that can be tamed and used to assist in combat with most hostile mobs.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.zoglin.desc: A zoglin is an undead hostile mob created when a hoglin enters the Overworld or End. It never retreats or flees, and attacks players and almost all non-zoglin mobs indiscriminately, using the same tusk attack as its non-zombified counterpart.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.zombie.desc: Zombies are common undead hostile mobs that deal melee damage and occasionally attack in groups.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.zombie_horse.de: A zombie horse is an undead variant of the regular horse. Zombie horses appear to be the horse equivalent of zombies. Like zombies, zombie horses are green-skinned and their eyes are completely black.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.zombie_villager: A zombie villager is a variant of the zombie that can be cured into a normal villager using a golden apple while it is under the effect of Weakness.
skada.bestiary.minecraft.zombified_pigli: A zombified piglin is a neutral undead variant of the piglin that inhabits the Nether. Zombified piglins normally ignore players, but if one is attacked, it and all zombified piglins in the vicinity become enraged and attack the aggressor with their golden swords.
